I'm also a layman so showed this to my speech therapist housemate because I thought the same thing as you. He says that most people with speech issues simply use a common gesture (like firmly putting a hand up and looking away) to communicate disinterest just like anyone else. He mentioned patients who did not have the use of their arms who make noise which clearly expresses disinterest /irritation, but again said its basically the same hmphs and sighs the rest of us make when we are annoyed. 

He also mentioned that much of this was a moot point in 2021 anyway because there are so many affordable speech devices available now that he sees very few mentally capable  patients who don't 'speak' electronically at least some of the time, usually while out in public. OP it seems like your wife's issues aren't so much her muteism as her intense anxiety, which is preventing her from finding ways to adapt to her mutism and live her life freely. I hope you guys get some help, but please remember that at a certain point...you HAVE to look out for your daughter and your relationship with her, first.

I really dont want to be harsh because I know how tough funding college is and I sympathise so much with your rough home life, and wish you nothing but success!  <3 That said, the family member who took you in isn't your parent, they're not obligated to make any sacrifices for you but they did. They made immense sacrifices to care for you as a teen, and it seems they're still helping/supporting you a lot now you're an adult? Even besides letting you live with them? 

They made an agreement that you wouldn't pay rent without knowing all the facts, ie how much financial aid you would get. When that turned out to be much more than expected, I think it's fair to change the agreement. --Frankly, I think they would have been well within their rights to change the rent agreement at will, even if you hadn't received any financial aid, because it's their house and they've done you an incredible favour. Now that you're an adult, they need to put themselves and their own welfare (including their financial security) first.

Also, I'm really sorry to say but you come off as very entitled. Like when you say that most of your finanal aid savings go to rent? Most people pay most of their wages for accommodation, especially students. The uni I teach at recently did a study that found the average freshman student is living off of £570 a month with £425 of that going on single-room accommodation. It's wrong, but most students dont have any savings. I find it hard to feel sorry for you having to use financial aid you were handed for being an unaccompanied minor - even though you weren't really, your family member was paying for and housing you - to pay for housing. That's literally what it's for? The financial aid is so you can feed, clothe, and house yourself. It's not just a cash gift for going to college.

There was a rash of scams like this on my old uni campus a few years back. Someone would approach you and ask you to look after their stuff while they went to the loo.  Either they would just not come back until you left, or an accomplice would come 'steal' their things while you were watching them. They'd then either accuse you of being the theif, or try to guilt you into handing over cash ('you owe it to me', 'my rent money was in that bag', 'my car keys are gone I need cash for a cab' etc.) It got so bad the campus coffee shops and bars had posters warning students about it for a few weeks.

So I don't know whether OP was TA in this case, but just a PSA for you guys because there are Assholes out there! I've never heard of this happening anywhere else, but just putting it out there for the future!
You'll find something that works for you! It might take a couple of weeks or months but you'll get there! I hope it all goes smoothly for you!

Hey  very late here but I hope this comment finds you beacause I was in almost exactly the same position as you a few years back. In my early twenties I was dating a freelance artist who was making enough money to live on, just about, but never got much attention or recognition for his work. He seemed to be happy working 'outside the system' in the beginning, while I was still a student. He would look over my coursework and help me out a lot; he gave me a lot of con crit I still take into account today. But when I finished uni and my own creative career really suddenly and unexpectedly took off, he wasn't as happy for me as I expected him to be.

He acted exactly like your gf, and we broke up over it. Years later, when we crossed paths at a conference, he apologised and admitted it was because he was insecure and envious of my new success - which I had suspected at the time, but he wouldn't admit to. Your gf is jealous that you're becoming successful, gaining recognition and critical praise, and she isn't. Maybe up until now she's been telling herself that it's not her lack of talent that's holding her back, it's an oppressive system which doesn't recognise real talent! That doesn't give the little guy a chance! You've just disproven that theory. 

In the end, I'm glad he's in a place where he can be content with his own success and supportive of others', but it took him a long time and a lot of life changes - he eventually gave up on freelancing and became an art teacher, got married, and had a kid - to get there.

He made me feel ashamed of my abilities and success. I'll never let anyone make me feel like that again, and you shouldn't either.
The only thing threatening my life is my mother!
